style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The psalm Jesus died praying. Into Your hand I entrust my spirit -- David's line for depositing his life with the God who had already redeemed it -- became the Son's last words on the cross, and Stephen's, and the church's deathbed prayer ever since. Around that line the psalm moves in waves, the way a bad season does: refuge and rescue, then a lament so complete that he is a reproach to enemies, a dread to friends, forgotten like a dead man, a cracked pot thrown out, hearing whispers and 'terror on every side' -- the phrase Jeremiah borrowed. The turn is three Hebrew words: You are my God. Then the psalm's other famous line, my times are in Your hand -- every season on the calendar held by the same hand that holds the spirit -- and a prayer for the shining face of the Aaronic blessing. It ends in public thanksgiving: how abundant is the goodness You have stored up for those who fear You; You hide them in the shelter of Your presence from the strife of tongues. He admits he had said in his panic, I am cut off from before Your eyes -- and that God heard him anyway. Love the LORD, all His faithful; be strong and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for Him. The Te Deum ends on this psalm's first verse.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of David. In You, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame; in Your righteousness rescue me.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. In You, O LORD [YHWH], do I put my trust [chasah -- take refuge]; let me never [al olam] be ashamed [bosh]: deliver [palat] me in Your righteousness [tsedaqah].
1.notes: bekha YHWH chasiti (H3068, H2620): in You I have taken refuge -- Psalm 11:1's opening, and the line the Te Deum ends on ('In te, Domine, speravi: non confundar in aeternum'); al-eboshah le-olam (H408, H954, H5769): let me not be shamed FOREVER -- be-tsidqatekha palleteni (H6666, H6403): in Your righteousness bring me out. Psalm 71:1-3 reuses these first three verses almost word for word.

2.text: Bend Your ear to me; rescue me quickly; be to me a rock of strength, a fortress-house to save me.
2.amp: Bow down [natah] Your ear [ozen] to me; deliver [natsal -- snatch] me speedily [meherah]: be You my strong rock ['to me for a rock of strength', tsur maoz, the KJV margin], for an house [bayith] of defence [metsudah -- fortress] to save [yasha] me.
2.notes: hatteh elai oznekha meherah hatsileni (H5186, H241, H4120, H5337): tilt Your ear -- rescue me FAST; heyeh li le-tsur-maoz (H6697, H4581): be to me 'for a rock of strength', the margin's literal -- le-bet metsudot le-hoshieni (H1004, H4686, H3467): for a house of fortresses to save me. Rock, stronghold, fortress-house: David the fugitive's vocabulary from the wilderness of Judah.

3.text: For You are my crag and my fortress; for Your name's sake You will lead me and guide me.
3.amp: For You are my rock [sela -- crag] and my fortress [metsudah]; therefore for Your name's [shem] sake lead [nachah] me, and guide [nahal -- lead to rest] me.
3.notes: ki-sali u-metsudati attah (H5553, H4686): my sela -- the crag, a different rock-word from verse 2's tsur -- and my fortress You are; u-le-maan shimkha tanchemi u-tenahaleni (H8034, H5148, H5095): for Your NAME's sake lead me and guide me -- Psalm 23:2-3's two shepherd verbs, nachah and nahal, and the same warrant: His name. The request rests on God's reputation, not David's.

4.text: You will pull me out of the net they hid for me, for You are my stronghold.
4.amp: Pull me out [yatsa -- bring me out] of the net [resheth] that [zu] they have laid privily [taman -- hidden] for me: for You are my strength [maoz -- stronghold].
4.notes: totsieni me-reshet zu tamenu li (H3318, H7568, H2098, H2934): bring me out of the net they hid for me -- Psalm 9:15's net, now around the psalmist's own foot; ki-attah mauzzi (H4581): for You are my maoz, my stronghold. The one in the net does not cut himself free; he names the One who can.

5.text: Into Your hand I entrust my spirit; You have redeemed me, O LORD, God of truth.
5.amp: Into Your hand [yad] I commit [paqad -- deposit, entrust] my spirit [ruach]: You have redeemed [padah -- ransomed] me, O LORD [YHWH] God [El] of truth [emeth -- faithfulness].
5.notes: be-yadekha aphqid ruchi (H3027, H6485, H7307): into Your hand I DEPOSIT my spirit -- paqad, which carries the sense of placing something in trusted hands -- the line Jesus prayed as His last words (Luke 23:46), adding 'Father' and dropping nothing else; Stephen turned it to Him (Acts 7:59), and it has been the deathbed prayer of the church since. paditah oti YHWH El emet (H6299, H3068, H410, H571): You have RANSOMED me, LORD, God of truth -- in David's mouth a rescue already done; in the Son's, the redemption He was accomplishing. The psalm's most famous line is also its logic: you can deposit your life with the One who has already bought it.

6.text: I hate those who cling to worthless idols, but as for me, I trust in the LORD.
6.amp: I have hated [sane] them that regard [shamar -- keep to] lying [shav -- empty] vanities [hebel -- breaths, idols]: but I trust [batach] in the LORD [YHWH].
6.notes: saneti ha-shomerim hable-shav (H8130, H8104, H1892, H7723): I hate those who KEEP the empty breaths -- hable-shav, vapors of nothing, the prophets' name for idols; Jonah prays this line from the fish (Jonah 2:8) -- va-ani el-YHWH batachti (H3068, H982): but I, toward the LORD I have trusted. The hatred is of a false hope, not of the people holding it; the contrast is what one leans on.

7.text: I will exult and rejoice in Your covenant love, because You have seen my affliction; You have known the distresses of my soul,
7.amp: I will be glad [gil -- exult] and rejoice [samach] in Your mercy [chesed -- covenant love]: for You have considered [raah -- seen] my trouble [oni -- affliction]; You have known [yada] my soul [nephesh] in adversities [tsarah];
7.notes: agilah ve-esmechah be-chasdekha (H1523, H8055, H2617): exult and rejoice in Your chesed -- the same pair of verbs as Psalm 9:2 -- asher raita et-onyi (H7200, H6040): because You SAW my affliction, Exodus 3:7's verb for the God who saw Egypt; yadata be-tsarot naphshi (H3045, H6869, H5315): You KNEW my soul in its distresses. Seen and known: the two things a suffering man most wants to be, and the two things God is said to have done.

8.text: and You have not handed me over to the enemy; You have set my feet in a wide open place.
8.amp: And have not shut me up [sagar -- delivered up] into the hand [yad] of the enemy [oyeb]: You have set [amad] my feet [regel] in a large room [merchab -- a broad place].
8.notes: ve-lo hisgartani be-yad-oyeb (H5462, H3027, H341): You did not SHUT me into the enemy's hand -- sagar, the word for handing a fugitive over (1 Samuel 23:11-12, Keilah, where it nearly happened). heemadta ba-merchab raglai (H5975, H4800, H7272): You stood my feet in the merchab, the wide place -- Psalm 18:19's room to move, the opposite of the net (v. 4) and the siege (v. 21).

9.text: Be gracious to me, O LORD, for I am in distress; my eye is wasted with grief -- my soul and my body too.
9.amp: Have mercy [chanan -- be gracious] upon me, O LORD [YHWH], for I am in trouble [tsarar -- hemmed in]: mine eye [ayin] is consumed with grief [kaas -- vexation], yea, my soul [nephesh] and my belly [beten -- body].
9.notes: chonneni YHWH ki tsar-li (H2603, H3068, H6887): be gracious -- 'it is narrow to me', the literal for distress, the opposite of verse 8's wide place; asheshah be-khaas eni naphshi u-bitni (H3708, H5869, H5315, H990): my eye has wasted with grief, my soul and my belly too -- Psalm 6:7's eye. The thanksgiving of verses 7-8 gives way to a lament again: the psalm moves in waves, as a real bad week does.

10.text: For my life is spent with sorrow and my years with groaning; my strength stumbles because of my iniquity, and my bones waste away.
10.amp: For my life [chay] is spent [kalah -- used up] with grief [yagon -- sorrow], and my years [shanah] with sighing [anachah -- groaning]: my strength [koach] fails [kashal -- stumbles] because of mine iniquity [avon], and my bones [etsem] are consumed.
10.notes: ki khalu be-yagon chayyai u-shenotai ba-anachah (H3615, H3015, H2416, H8141, H585): life used up in sorrow, years in groaning. kashal ba-avoni khochi (H3782, H5771, H3581): my strength STUMBLES 'in my iniquity' -- the psalm's one confession: some of this trouble is his own doing, and he says so (the ancient Greek read 'in my affliction'; the Hebrew has avon). va-atsamai asheshu (H6106): and my bones waste. Psalm 32:3's bones.

11.text: Because of all my adversaries I have become a reproach, and to my neighbors most of all, and a dread to my acquaintances; those who see me in the street run from me.
11.amp: I was a reproach [cherpah] among all mine enemies [tsarar -- adversaries], but especially [meod] among my neighbours, and a fear [pachad -- dread] to mine acquaintance [yada]: they that did see [raah] me without [chuts -- in the street] fled [nadad] from me.
11.notes: mi-kol-tsorerai hayiti cherpah ve-li-shekhenai meod (H6887, H2781, H3966): from all my adversaries I became a reproach -- and to my neighbors 'exceedingly'; u-phachad li-meyuddaai (H6343, H3045): a DREAD to those who knew me -- roai ba-chuts nadedu mimmenni (H7200, H2351, H5074): people who saw me in the street bolted. Psalm 38:11 and Job 19:13-19 know the scene; so does the Man of Sorrows (Isaiah 53:3).

12.text: I am forgotten like a dead man, out of mind; I have become like a broken pot.
12.amp: I am forgotten [shakach] as a dead man [muth] out of mind [leb -- heart]: I am like a broken ['a vessel that perisheth', abad, the KJV margin] vessel [keli].
12.notes: nishkachti ke-met mi-leb (H7911, H4191, H3820): forgotten like a dead man 'from the heart' -- out of everyone's mind; hayiti ki-khli obed (H3627, H6): I have become like a keli obed, 'a vessel that perishes', the margin's literal -- a cracked pot thrown out (cf. Jeremiah 22:28). The middle of the psalm is its bottom.

13.text: For I have heard the whispering of many -- terror on every side! -- as they conspire together against me and plot to take my life.
13.amp: For I have heard [shama] the slander [dibbah -- whispering] of many [rab]: fear [magor -- terror] was on every side: while they took counsel [yasad -- sat in council] together [yachad] against me, they devised [zamam -- plotted] to take away [laqach] my life [nephesh].
13.notes: ki shamati dibbat rabbim magor mi-sabib (H8085, H1681, H7227, H4032): I have heard the whisper of many -- 'terror on every side', magor missabib, the phrase Jeremiah made a nickname (Jeremiah 20:3, 10), and he seems to be quoting this psalm. be-hivvasedam yachad alai laqachat naphshi zamamu (H3245, H3162, H3947, H5315, H2161): as they sat in council together against me, they plotted to take my life. Slander, then conspiracy, then the plan: the psalm knows the sequence.

14.text: But as for me, I trust in You, O LORD; I have said, 'You are my God.'
14.amp: But I trusted [batach] in You, O LORD [YHWH]: I said [amar], You are my God [Elohim].
14.notes: va-ani alekha batachti YHWH (H982, H3068): 'but I' -- the pivot pronoun of verse 6 again -- on You I have trusted; amarti Elohai attah (H559, H430): I have said, 'my God are You'. The shortest creed in the Psalter, spoken from the bottom of verse 12: three Hebrew words, and the whole turn of the psalm hangs on them.

15.text: My times are in Your hand; rescue me from the hand of my enemies and from those who hunt me.
15.amp: My times [et] are in Your hand [yad]: deliver [natsal -- snatch] me from the hand [yad] of mine enemies [oyeb], and from them that persecute [radaph -- pursue] me.
15.notes: be-yadekha ittotai (H3027, H6256): my TIMES -- ittot, the plural: every season, every turn of circumstance, the good years and the bad -- are in Your hand, the hand the spirit was deposited in (v. 5); hatsileni mi-yad-oyebai u-me-rodephai (H5337, H3027, H341, H7291): snatch me from the hand of my enemies and my pursuers. Two hands in one verse; the psalmist knows which one holds the calendar.

16.text: Make Your face shine on Your servant; save me in Your covenant love.
16.amp: Make Your face [panim] to shine [or] upon Your servant [ebed]: save [yasha] me for Your mercies' [chesed -- covenant love] sake.
16.notes: hairah phanekha al-abdekha (H215, H6440, H5650): make Your face SHINE on Your servant -- the Aaronic blessing's second line (Numbers 6:25), prayed by the one being blessed; hoshieni be-chasdekha (H3467, H2617): save me in Your chesed -- covenant love as the element the rescue happens in. After the hidden faces of verse 11, one face is asked to shine.

17.text: O LORD, let me not be put to shame, for I have called on You; let the wicked be put to shame; let them go silent in Sheol.
17.amp: Let me not be ashamed [bosh], O LORD [YHWH]; for I have called [qara] upon You: let the wicked [rasha] be ashamed [bosh], and let them be silent ['cut off for', damam, the KJV margin] in the grave [sheol].
17.notes: YHWH al-eboshah ki qeratikha (H3068, H954, H7121): verse 1's plea again -- let me not be shamed, because I have called on YOU -- the caller's honor is now the One called on. yeboshu reshaim yiddemu li-sheol (H954, H7563, H1826, H7585): let the wicked be shamed, let them be SILENT for Sheol -- damam, still, dumb; the margin's 'cut off'. The men of the whispering (v. 13) asked to go quiet in the grave.

18.text: Let lying lips be struck dumb -- lips that speak insolently against the righteous with pride and contempt.
18.amp: Let the lying [sheqer] lips [saphah] be put to silence [alam -- struck dumb]; which speak [dabar] hard things proudly [gaavah -- arrogance] and contemptuously [buz -- contempt] against the righteous [tsaddiq].
18.notes: teallamnah siphte shaqer (H481, H8193, H8267): let the lying lips be struck DUMB -- alam, the word for Ezekiel's bound tongue (Ezekiel 3:26); ha-doberot al-tsaddiq ataq be-gaavah va-buz (H1696, H6662, H6277, H1346, H937): that speak against the righteous 'a hard thing', the margin's literal -- insolence -- with pride and contempt. Psalm 12:3's prayer against the smooth tongue, here against the hard one.

19.text: How abundant is Your goodness, which You have stored up for those who fear You, which You have worked out for those who take refuge in You, in front of the children of men!
19.amp: Oh how great [rab -- abundant] is Your goodness [tov], which You have laid up [tsaphan -- stored, treasured] for them that fear [yare] You; which You have wrought [paal] for them that trust [chasah -- take refuge] in You before the sons [ben] of men [adam]!
19.notes: mah rab-tubekha asher-tsaphanta li-reekha (H7227, H2898, H6845, H3373): how ABUNDANT Your goodness -- tub, the goodness Moses was shown passing by (Exodus 33:19) -- which You have STORED UP, tsaphan, laid by like treasure, for those who fear You. paalta la-chosim bakh neged bene adam (H6466, H2620, H1121, H120): worked out for those taking refuge in You -- in front of the sons of men. Goodness in two places: stored in reserve, and already shown in public.

20.text: You hide them in the shelter of Your presence from the plots of men; You keep them safe in a pavilion from the strife of tongues.
20.amp: You shall hide [satar] them in the secret [sether -- hiding place] of Your presence [panim -- face] from the pride of man [ish]: You shall keep them secretly [tsaphan -- treasure them away] in a pavilion [sukkah -- booth] from the strife [rib] of tongues [lashon].
20.notes: tastirem be-seter panekha me-rukhse ish (H5641, H5643, H6440, H7407, H376): You hide them in the SECRET of Your face -- the hiding place is God's own presence -- from the plottings of man. titspenem be-sukkah me-rib leshonot (H6845, H5521, H7379, H3956): You treasure them away -- the same tsaphan as verse 19 -- in a sukkah, a booth, from the strife of tongues. The whispering of verse 13 cannot get into that tent (cf. Psalm 27:5).

21.text: Blessed be the LORD, for He has shown me wonderful covenant love in a city under siege.
21.amp: Blessed [barak] be the LORD [YHWH]: for He has showed me His marvellous [pala -- wonderful] kindness [chesed -- covenant love] in a strong ['fenced', ir, the KJV margin] city [ir].
21.notes: barukh YHWH ki hiphli chasdo li (H1288, H3068, H6381, H2617): blessed be the LORD -- He made His chesed WONDERFUL to me, Psalm 17:7's verb. be-ir matsor (H5892, H4692): in a 'fenced city', the margin -- a city under siege, or a fortified one: Keilah (1 Samuel 23) or Ziklag, or simply the tight place of verse 9. Covenant love arrived inside the walls.

22.text: As for me, I said in my alarm, 'I am cut off from before Your eyes!' -- and yet You heard the voice of my pleas for grace when I cried to You for help.
22.amp: For I said [amar] in my haste [chaphaz -- alarm, panic], I am cut off from before [neged] Your eyes [ayin]: nevertheless [aken -- surely] You heard [shama] the voice [qol] of my supplications [tachanun -- pleas for grace] when I cried [shava] unto You.
22.notes: va-ani amarti be-chophzi nigrazti mi-neged enekha (H559, H2648, H1629, H5048, H5869): 'and I' -- I said in my panic, chaphaz, the word for a rout (Psalm 116:11 says its 'all men are liars' in the same panic) -- 'I am CUT OFF from before Your eyes'. akhen shamata qol tachanunai be-shavvei elekha (H403, H8085, H6963, H8469, H7768): NEVERTHELESS You heard the voice of my pleas when I shouted to You. The panic was wrong and the prayer was heard anyway: the psalm's whole comfort is in that 'nevertheless'.

23.text: Love the LORD, all you His faithful ones! The LORD preserves the faithful and pays back in full the one who acts in pride.
23.amp: O love [ahab] the LORD [YHWH], all you His saints [chasid -- covenant-loyal ones]: for the LORD [YHWH] preserves [natsar -- guards] the faithful [aman -- the trustworthy], and plentifully [yether -- in full measure] rewards [shalam -- repays] the proud [gaavah] doer [asah].
23.notes: ehebu et-YHWH kol-chasidav (H157, H3068, H2623): LOVE the LORD, all His chasidim -- the psalm turns to the congregation, as thanksgivings do; emunim notser YHWH (H539, H5341, H3068): the LORD GUARDS the faithful -- u-meshallem al-yeter oseh gaavah (H7999, H3499, H6213, H1346): and repays 'with surplus' the doer of pride. Two ledgers, both kept exactly.

24.text: Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who wait in hope for the LORD.
24.amp: Be of good courage [chazaq -- be strong], and He shall strengthen [amats -- make bold] your heart [lebab], all you that hope [yachal -- wait expectantly] in the LORD [YHWH].
24.notes: chizqu ve-yaamets lebabkhem (H2388, H553, H3824): be strong, and let your heart be bold -- the two verbs of Joshua's commissioning (Joshua 1:6-9), here for anyone who prays; kol-ha-meyachalim la-YHWH (H3176, H3068): all who WAIT for the LORD -- yachal, hope as waiting. Psalm 27:14 ends the same way; a man who has been in the net, the siege, and the panic tells the rest of the church what he learned there.
